A Hidden Gem with Stunning Views and Great Value! We recently visited Nook, and it truly lived up to its reputation. The restaurant is situated on a large property right at the edge of a stunning rice field, offering that iconic, peaceful Bali vibe that everyone looks for. The menu is incredibly diverse, catering to all tastes with impressive vegetarian and meat options. We were particularly intrigued by their specialty burgers—trying the black bun burger for the first time was a highlight! The presentation was top-notch and the quality of the ingredients was evident. Commonly praised by many visitors—and we totally agree—is the relaxing atmosphere and the seamless service. Whether you prefer the smoking or non-smoking section, the layout feels breezy and comfortable. Also, having a dedicated parking area right in front is a huge plus in this area. We paid approximately 300,000 IDR for two burger sets and a Bintang, which is excellent value for money considering the premium location and high-quality service. It’s the perfect spot for a casual yet high-quality meal with a view. Highly recommended!

Review:
Stopped by Tempong Indra for dinner, one of the popular local food spots in Bali. I’d give this place a 7.8/10. The food is tasty and filling, but the price feels quite expensive compared to other Indonesian dishes with similar portions. One serving of nasi tempong ayam includes fried chicken, rice, tempe, and vegetables—simple Indonesian comfort food. We ordered 2 nasi tempong ayam and 2 iced teas, and spent around IDR 150,000, which is definitely on the pricey side for this kind of meal. Important note: the sambal is extremely spicy 🔥 Even for those who are used to spicy food, it really packs a punch. If you’re not a big fan of spicy food, it’s better to ask for less sambal or have it served separately. Overall, Tempong Indra is worth a try for sambal lovers, but for Indonesian budget travelers, expect higher prices and very intense spice levels.

The place itself was beautiful... downstairs had this vibey bar seating, while upstairs gave you the option of indoor coziness or breezy outdoor tables. I’ve tried some of Asia’s Top 50 bars, and sometimes the drinks sound fancy but taste like a confused science experiment. Here though, every cocktail felt Michelin-level. Imagine sipping bourbon with a subtle peanut finish, or a lemongrass cocktail spiked with curry leaves... sounds odd, but it was magic. We left really grateful for the whole experience. It felt extra special since it doubled as our little celebration after completing the Maybank Bali Full Marathon. This place is a gem... I’m pretty sure in a few months you’ll need to book weeks in advance.

The taste still remain faithful but I find the soup to be too sweet for my liking now. Instead, I would very much opt for the clear broth for my next visit. The deep fried fish fillet were okay. They come in sizeable chunks and you're lucky if you get the freshly fried crispy batch. Mine however was not and so it turned out to be tough. Nothing much to comment about the other options of items as they're quite standard. Overall I wouldn't say that this is a fantastic tomyam mee but instead, a bowl of comfort food be it on a rainy day or for late night cravings.

Visited on a Sunday afternoon around lunch time and the place was crowded with a short line of 5-6 parties lining up outside. As we were a couple, we didn't have to wait too long (10-15 min). We were pleasantly surprised that the prices were very wallet friendly, as we were expecting it to be wildly expensive for a well-established restaurant like this one. We got a Tom yum soup, som tum, basil pork, pad see ew and Thai ice milk tea (not pictured) Unfortunately I didn't not take a photo of the menu, and I can't recall how much we spent on this meal. It was definitely affordable for a meal of this proportion. The service was quick and my ice milk tea arrived shortly. I found the tea taste to be strong, combined with the milky condensed milk and evaporated milk. However it was a tad too sweet for liking. The somtum was delicious, with the right amount of spice and tang to whet your appetite. The crunchy texture of the veg provided an excellent contrast to the pad see ew I had. The rice noodles were stir fried with a proper wok, smoky and savoury. The Tom yum soup was creamy, sour and spicy. There were plenty of fresh ingredients such as mushrooms and seafood. My partner had the basil pork rice and said it was an okay plate. But would have preferred more basil and for it to be less wet (his personal preference). Overall we had a good meal at Inter Restaurant, would recommend for anyone who's nearby and looking a good lunch spot that has a wide menu of Thai food.

Review:
We arrived at Ar Restaurant around 3:30pm local time, after a long travel to Hatyai. It was just a short walk from our hotel. We were famished, as we hadn't had our lunch yet. Luckily, the restaurant was practically empty when we arrived, so the food was served quickly after we placed our orders. First up was the medium sized Seafood Tom Yum. The soup was rich and flavourful, and the spiciness and sourness was just nice. The seafood tasted great too. The medium sized portion was just right for the 4 of us. Then came Stir Fried Asparagus with Prawns, with king oyster mushrooms in it as well. Simple yet tasty. Up next was Spicy Petai with Squid. Squid were cooked with the petai beans, along with chillies and basil leaves. It was very delicious and makes me want to eat more rice with it. Last to be served was the Deep Fried Pork Knuckle. The pork knuckle was covered with delicious crackling, which was very easy to eat even for the elders in the group, due to its crispiness. The meat was tender, and I especially enjoyed the tendon of the pork knuckle, the jelly like substance that was both flavour packed and succulent. My gf loved the dish, even though she doesn't normally enjoy eating meat. While it was already great to eat on its own, we also enjoyed the green dipping sauce that came with it, which had a balanced level of spiciness from the chilli and sourness from the lime juice. For drinks, they offered a choice of bottled drinking water and sugarcane drink in a bottle. We opted for the sugarcane drink, but while it was too sweet for my taste, the sweetness was a great way to balance the spiciness in the food. Overall, great food, reasonably priced. I would recommend giving this place a try, especially for their pork knuckle.

Review:
Lovely old and traditional restaurant serving Thai-Chinese fusion cuisine. Its located inside a very well-preserved old heritage building. We ordered various of their signature dishes and all of them were pretty good, with a few standout dishes. The best dishes were the deep fried pork knuckles and salted fish kailan vege. The pork knuckle is crispy on the outside, and very soft and tender on the inside, the meat literally melts in your mouth. I highly recommend pairing the meat with the sweet soy sauce that comes with it, absolutely delicious! For salted fish kailan lovers, their rendition is very good. The kailan is not too hard, and not bitter at all. Moreover, the salted fish is very fragrant and flavorful. Highly recommend these 2 dishes! Some other decent dishes include their tomyum, which is super flavourful and spicy, and the thai-style water spinach. Their crab-based dishes are pretty interesting as they use whole crab meats as the ingredients, which includes the cartilage and sometimes crab shells. It's very annoying to pick away the cartilage and randomly bite into a shell while eating the crab fried rice and egg. However, the taste of those dishes are still pretty good. Dishes we found slightly underwhelming (but still good) are the shrimp rolls and oyster omelette. The shrimp roll tasted pretty bland without much of a shrimp taste. While the oyster omelette is also pretty bland, I very much prefer the Penang style oyster omelette instead unfortunately. Overall, it's still an incredible restaurant right in the town center and I highly recommend to try it out you love Thai-Chinese fusion food.
